cases.event: One spring, messages sent from a weather sensor at the fictional {E} began arriving with wrong numbers.
cases.q: What most likely caused the messages from {E} to arrive with wrong numbers?
restate: Messages from {E} began arriving with wrong numbers, and the question asks why.
Something made the messages from {E} arrive with mistakes.
cases.answer: Electrical interference from a new pump motor most likely caused the errors, because it flipped some of the 1s in the messages to 0s as they traveled through the cable.
cases.sum: the evidence points to interference from the pump motor as the reason the messages arrived with wrong numbers.
cases.myth: The messages from {E} arrived wrong because the numbers got tired during the trip.
cases.mythClause: errors appeared only in messages about rain
cases.altText: Some students suggested that the weather sensor at {E} was broken.
cases.patternQ: What pattern connects the pump motor and the message errors at {E}?
cases.patternA: Errors appeared after the motor was installed next to the cable and stopped once the cable was moved away, so the errors followed the motor.
cases.patternSum: the errors appeared after the motor was installed next to the cable and stopped once the cable was moved away.

prediction.text: When the errors began, a student predicted that they would happen at random times of day.
prediction.claim: the errors at {E} would happen at random times of day
prediction.whyNot: the errors appeared only during the hours when the motor was running

cases.observerNote: The technicians saved a copy of every message.

obs.text: The errors began the same week a large water pump motor was installed beside the data cable at {E}.
exps: the errors started right when the motor arrived, which points to the motor as the cause
the timing ties the errors to the new motor, not to the sensor
a change that appears the week a motor is installed suggests the motor caused it

obs.text: Tests showed that whenever the motor ran, some 1s in the messages from {E} arrived as 0s.
exps: a 1 that turns into a 0 changes the number the message stands for, which explains the wrong values
this shows how the motor caused the errors, since its electrical noise flipped digits in the cable
flipped digits are exactly the kind of damage interference would cause

obs.text: When the cable was moved {n0} meters away from the motor, the errors stopped.
obs.tag: the cable after it was moved
exps: the errors stopped once the cable was away from the motor, which is what would happen if the motor were the cause
separating the cable from the motor fixed the problem, so the two are linked
once the cause was moved away, the effect disappeared

obs.text: A technician checked the sensor's readings on its own screen at {E}, and they were correct.
exps: if the sensor itself were broken, its own screen would show wrong numbers too
this rules out a broken sensor, because its readings were correct before they were sent
with the sensor working, the broken-sensor explanation has nothing to stand on

obs.text: Errors appeared only during the hours when the motor at {E} was running.
exps: a broken sensor would make mistakes all day, but the errors followed the motor's schedule
this rules out the sensor, since the errors matched the motor's hours
errors that start and stop with the motor point to the motor, not the sensor
predExps: this directly contradicts the prediction, since the errors followed the motor's schedule instead of happening at random
if the errors were random, they would appear at any hour, but they did not
the prediction expected a random pattern, and the observations show a clear schedule
